angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 6,766,378 km at 135.94 pc = 0.67 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: distance 135.938 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.082), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 135.938 +/- 11.147 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 7.2345 +/- 0.0294 mas (same row, RUWE 1.18), 245.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 9.726 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: radius 9.726 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 45.227 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.097) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 6,766,378 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4803 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: effective temperature 4803 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.132) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56508: effective temperature 4803 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.132) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.86 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 7 published values span log g 2.39 to 2.858, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
